title: TRACE: Trajectory-Routed Causal Memory for Delayed-Evidence Visuomotor Imitation
abstract: arXiv:2606.14551v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Robots under autonomous operation may require decisions based on evidence that is no longer visible. We study delayed-evidence tasks, where an early cue disappears before a later decision point, so visually similar observations can require different actions. In these settings, the current observation is not a sufficient state for control. We introduce TRAjectory-routed Causal Evidence (TRACE), a memory framework for visuomotor imitation policies. TRACE stores task-relevant visual and robot-state evidence, such as object identity, target choice, or route-dependent state, in a fixed-size latent memory that remains bounded over long episodes. Instead of indexing memory by raw time or manually provided task labels, TRACE uses path signatures: compact, order-sensitive features of the executed robot-state trajectory. translated_title: TRACE：面向延迟证据视觉运动模仿的轨迹路由因果记忆
translated_abstract: 自主运行中的机器人可能需要基于已经不可见的证据做出决策。我们研究延迟证据任务，即早期线索在后续决策点到来之前消失，因此视觉上相似的观测可能需要执行不同的动作。在这类场景中，当前观测不足以作为控制的充分状态。我们提出了轨迹路由因果证据（TRACE），这是一个面向视觉运动模仿策略的记忆框架。TRACE将任务相关的视觉与机器人状态证据（如物体身份、目标选择或依赖路径的状态）存储在一个固定大小的潜在记忆中，该记忆在长时程任务中始终保持有界。TRACE不使用原始时间或人工提供的任务标签来索引记忆，而是采用路径签名——即所执行机器人状态轨迹的紧凑且顺序敏感的特征。这些签名并不存储视觉线索本身，而是为记忆的写入与读取提供轨迹条件化的键。
tldr: TRACE提出了一种以机器人状态轨迹的路径签名作为记忆索引键的固定大小因果记忆框架，使视觉运动模仿策略能够基于早已消失的早期视觉证据正确完成延迟决策任务。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a fixed-size causal memory framework that uses path signatures of robot-state trajectories as indexing keys, enabling visuomotor imitation policies to act correctly on early visual evidence that is no longer visible in delayed-evidence tasks.
